description: A destructive foliar disease affecting cucurbit crops worldwide. It causes yellow leaf lesions and rapid leaf death, reducing plant growth and fruit yield. Severe outbreaks can cause major crop losses.
symptoms: Angular yellow or chlorotic spots on leaves
Lesions limited by leaf veins (especially on cucumber)
Gray to purple fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves
Lesions enlarge and become brown or necrotic
Reduced canopy leading to sunburn and fruit damage
favorable_conditions: Frequent rain or long leaf wetness
Dense plant canopy with poor airflow
spread: Long-distance airborne spread from infected regions
infection_process: Spores land on wet leaf surfaces
Hyphae grow inside leaf tissue and extract nutrients
management: Use tolerant or resistant cultivars when available
Improve airflow through plant spacing and pruning
Monitor crops regularly for early symptoms
Use forecasting systems to predict outbreaks
biological_control: Use microbial biopesticides such as Bacillus-based products
Encourage healthy soil microbiome to reduce disease pressure
chemical_control: Preventive fungicide sprays during high-risk periods
Apply fungicides every 5–7 days for cucumber or 7–10 days for other cucurbits during outbreaks
Rotate fungicides with different modes of action to prevent resistance
Active ingredients may include metalaxyl alternatives, strobilurins, or other registered fungicides
prevention: Ensure good air circulation in fields
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness from irrigation
Use disease forecasting tools to time fungicide sprays
impact: Can cause yield losses up to 80–100% in severe outbreaks
Major threat to cucurbit production worldwide
source: Savory et al. – Molecular Plant Pathology
